judged_text: Blacklisted guest emails are silently filtered out of the request, and if filtering leaves zero guests the error surfaced is the misleading 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. A user who submits one blacklisted address among three sees 'Guests added' success and never learns one email was dropped; a user whose entire submission was filtered is told their emails were invalid/duplicate, sending them debugging the wrong problem.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklisted emails are filtered out via `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(... && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))` with no user-facing feedback. If all submitted guests are filtered out, the handler throws `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which is misleading because the failure can be due solely to blacklist filtering (not invalid/duplicate emails). If only some are blacklisted, the mutation still succeeds and the UI shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`, so the user is never told some inputs were dropped.
